readings.title: Gangra (fourth century): Canon I
readings.text:
Canon I.

If any one shall condemn marriage, or abominate and condemn a woman who is a believer and devout, and sleeps with her own husband, as though she could not enter the Kingdom [of heaven] let him be anathema.

readings.title: Gangra (fourth century): Canon IV
readings.text:
Canon IV.

If any one shall maintain, concerning a married presbyter, that is not lawful to partake of the oblation when he offers it, let him be anathema.

readings.title: Gangra (fourth century): Canon IX
readings.text:
Canon IX.

If any one shall remain virgin, or observe continence, abstaining from marriage because he abhors it, and not on account of the beauty and holiness of virginity itself, let him be anathema.

readings.title: Gangra (fourth century): Canon X
readings.text:
Canon X.

If any one of those who are living a virgin life for the Lord's sake shall treat arrogantly the married, let him be anathema.

readings.text:
Canon XIV.

If any woman shall forsake her husband, and resolve to depart from him because she abhors marriage, let her be anathema.

readings.title: Gangra (fourth century): Canon XV
readings.text:
Canon XV.

If anyone shall forsake his own children and shall not nurture them, nor so far as in him lies, rear them in becoming piety, but shall neglect them, under pretence of asceticism, let him be anathema.

readings.title: Gangra (fourth century): Canon XVI
readings.text:
Canon XVI.

If, under any pretence of piety, any children shall forsake their parents, particularly [if the parents are] believers, and shall withhold becoming reverence from their parents, on the plea that they honour piety more than them, let them be anathema.

readings.title: Gangra: Epilogue
readings.locator: Synod of Gangra: Epilogue following Canon XX
readings.text: These things we write, not to cut off those who wish to lead in the Church of God an ascetic life, according to the Scriptures; but those who carry the pretence of asceticism to superciliousness; both exalting themselves above those who live more simply, and introducing novelties contrary to the Scriptures and the ecclesiastical Canons. We do, assuredly, admire virginity accompanied by humility; and we have regard for continence, accompanied by godliness and gravity; and we praise the leaving of worldly occupations, [when it is made] with lowliness of mind; [but at the same time] we honour the holy companionship of marriage, and we do not contemn wealth enjoyed with uprightness and beneficence; and we commend plainness and frugality in apparel, [which is worn] only from attention, [and that] not over-fastidious, to the body; but dissolute and effeminate excess in dress we eschew; and we reverence the houses of God and embrace the assemblies held therein as holy and helpful, not confining religion within the houses, but reverencing every place built in the name of God; and we approve of gathering together in the Church itself for the common profit; and we bless the exceeding charities done by the brethren to the poor, according to the traditions of the Church; and, to sum up in a word, we wish that all things which have been delivered by the Holy Scriptures and the Apostolical traditions, may be observed in the Church.
readings.context: Complete text of the named historical canon, without the volume’s subsequent editorial Notes. Local conciliar discipline is identified by council and number; this reading does not assign a present-day penance or infer that every historical detail applies identically in every parish. The volume distinguishes this epilogue from the 20 numbered canons, noting that some Greek commentators count it asXXI.

scripture.text:
Now concerning the things whereof ye wrote unto me: It is good for a man not to touch a woman.

Nevertheless, to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband.

Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.

The wife hath not power of her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband hath not power of his own body, but the wife.

Defraud ye not one the other, except it be with consent for a time, that ye may give yourselves to fasting and prayer; and come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency.

But I speak this by permission, and not of commandment.

For I would that all men were even as I myself. But every man hath his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that.

I say therefore to the unmarried and widows, It is good for them if they abide even as I.

But if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn.

overview.text: The canons of Gangra address claims of superior holiness that led some people to condemn marriage or neglect family responsibilities. Asceticism means disciplined abstinence or renunciation for religious ends. The council distinguishes such a life joined to humility from contempt for married Christians and abandonment of care.

readings.title: Can marriage be condemned as excluding salvation?

paragraphs.text: Canon I rejects condemning marriage or treating a devout married woman as unable to enter the kingdom because she lives with her husband. Its concern is the rejection of marriage as spiritually disqualifying. The anathema is the council’s formal rejection of that claim.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: Does a priest’s marriage invalidate his offering?

paragraphs.text: Canon IV rejects the claim that the oblation offered by a married presbyter cannot be received. Presbyter means priest, and oblation here means the sacramental offering. The canon addresses the stated objection to his married status.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: What motive for abstaining from marriage does the canon reject?

paragraphs.text: Canon IX distinguishes valuing virginity from abstaining because marriage is regarded with disgust. Its judgment concerns the latter motive. The council does not condemn the choice of a continent life in itself.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: How does the council address contempt toward married people?

paragraphs.text: Canon X rejects arrogance toward married Christians by someone living in virginity for the Lord’s sake. The issue is spiritual superiority and contempt. The canon places humility alongside the practice of abstinence.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: What kind of marital abandonment is condemned?

paragraphs.text: Canon XIV concerns leaving a husband because marriage itself is abhorred. Its wording identifies that particular ground. The canon is not a discussion of every circumstance in which spouses may be separated.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: Can ascetic claims excuse neglecting children?

paragraphs.text: Canon XV rejects abandoning children or refusing their nurture under a claim of asceticism. The specific concern is the removal of ordinary parental care in the name of religious renunciation. It relates the claimed practice to its consequences for dependents.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: Can a claim of piety excuse contempt for parents?

paragraphs.text: Canon XVI rejects forsaking parents and withholding fitting respect on the claim that religion is more important than such responsibility. The text especially names parents who are believers. Its judgment concerns religious pretence used to evade a familial obligation.
paragraphs.reason: The owner authorized a plain-English curriculum explanation so beginners can understand the topic before consulting the preserved source passage.

readings.title: What balance does the council’s conclusion state?

paragraphs.text: The epilogue honors virginity, continence, and renunciation joined to humility, while also honoring marriage, honest possessions used generously, church assemblies, and care for the poor. It explains that the canons target arrogance and innovations under the pretence of asceticism. They do not reject disciplined Christian life as such.
